name: Statistics
notes: Double majors with Economics or Business may substitute ECON 231W for STAT 216.
STAT 180 replaces the former STAT 212; STAT 190 replaces STAT 213 / DSCC 262.
STAT 219 counts as an applications course only for the Class of 2026 and earlier.

requirementGroups.label: Prerequisite: calculus sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following calculus sequences: MATH 161 and MATH 162; MATH 141, MATH 142, and MATH 143; MATH 171 and MATH 172

requirementGroups.label: Prerequisite: introductory statistics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following introductory statistics courses: STAT 180; STAT 190; ECON 230: Economic Statistics; PSCI 200: Data Analysis I

requirementGroups.label: Core courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Core Courses (Three Courses): STAT/MATH 201: Introduction to Probability; STAT/MATH 203: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics; STAT 216: Intermediate Statistical Methodology

requirementGroups.label: Computational courses (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Computational Courses (Two Courses). Choose two of the following: STAT 275(W): R Programming; STAT 276(W): Statistical Computation in R; STAT 277; CSC 171; CSC 172. It is highly recommended to have at least one STAT-listed computing course for the major.

requirementGroups.label: Methods courses (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Methods Courses (Two Courses). Choose two of the following: STAT 219: Nonparametric Inference; STAT 221W: Sampling Techniques; STAT 223: Bayesian Inference; STAT 226W: Linear Models

requirementGroups.label: Applications courses (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Applications Courses (Two Courses). Choose two of the following: STAT 215; STAT 217; STAT 218; STAT 219 (for students in the Class of 2026 and previous); DSCC 265

requirementGroups.label: Upper-level electives (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Upper-Level Elective Courses (Two Courses). Choose two of the following courses: Any non-introductory 200-level STAT course; MATH 202; MATH 208; MATH 209; MATH 217; MATH 218; PSCI 205; PSCI 281; PSCI 288; ECON 223; ECON 224
requirementGroups.note: 'Any non-introductory 200-level STAT course' is also allowed but not enumerated here.
